Kerala braces for heavy rain as red alert issued in five districts, schools closed
Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad will be under a red alert on October 25, while Idukki and Palakkad will be under the alert the following day.
Advertisement
Officials warned that intense rainfall over a short period could cause flash floods, overflowing streams, waterlogging in urban and low-lying areas, and landslides. (PTI Photo)
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued red alerts for extremely heavy rainfall in five Kerala districts on Sunday and Monday, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad will be under a red alert on October 25, while Idukki and Palakkad will be under the alert the following day.
An orange alert has been issued for Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod on Saturday, indicating the possibility of very heavy rainfall at isolated places.
Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki and Ernakulam will be under a yellow alert for heavy rainfall on Saturday.
The IMD classifies rainfall exceeding 204.4 mm in 24 hours as extremely heavy, rainfall between 115.6 mm and 204.4 mm as very heavy, and rainfall between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm as heavy.
In view of the alerts, the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) warned that intense rainfall over a short period could cause flash floods, overflowing streams, waterlogging in urban and low-lying areas, and landslides.
The authority advised people in landslide-prone hilly areas and flood-prone low-lying regions to move to safer places if necessary. It also asked people not to cross rivers or enter water bodies during heavy rain, avoid non-essential travel, and stay away from waterfalls and hilly areas until the warnings are withdrawn.
Night travel to hilly areas should be completely avoided, the KSDMA said in a social media post. It also urged the public and government agencies to remain vigilant.
Following the red alert, the Malappuram District Collector declared a holiday on Sunday for anganwadis, madrasas, tuition centres, parallel colleges and other coaching centres, PTI reported.
The Kozhikode District Collector also declared a holiday for educational institutions, including anganwadis, madrasas and tuition centres.
Authorities said the holiday would not apply to residential educational institutions and hostels, or to university and public examinations scheduled in advance.
Five Kerala districts will, therefore, face red alerts over two days, while several others remain under orange and yellow alerts. Authorities have asked residents to take precautions, avoid risky travel and remain vigilant during the period of heavy rainfall.

articles.full_text:
Buses are being operated only up to Mettupalayam from the Mettupalayam road bus stand in Coimbatore on Saturday as the Nilgiris district remain cut off owing to a series of landslips from Burliyar.
| Photo Credit: S. SIVA SARAVANAN
All tourist spots in the Nilgiris district have been ordered to remain closed until further notice, while the Coimbatore district administration has advised the public to avoid ghat roads connecting Mettupalayam with Udhagamandalam and Pollachi with Valparai, following heavy rain and landslides at several locations.
The Nilgiris District Collector Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru ordered the closure of tourist spots on Saturday (October 24) after the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for very heavy rainfall in the district on October 24 and 25. In a press release, she said heavy rain had resulted in trees falling across roads and landslides, disrupting traffic.
In a separate public safety advisory issued on Saturday, the Coimbatore district administration said the public should avoid the ghat roads from Mettupalayam to Udhagamandalam via Coonoor and Kotagiri, and from Pollachi to Valparai, as major landslides had occurred at several locations.
Vehicle movement, including Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) bus services, to the Nilgiris and Valparai has been stopped between 6 p.m. and 7 a.m. Essential and emergency vehicles are exempt from the restriction.
The administration has cautioned that heavy rain could result in trees falling across roads, landslides, rockfalls and sudden flooding. The public has been advised against visiting waterfalls, rivers, streams, dams, lakes and other water bodies, and asked to stay away from flooded roads, overflowing streams and low-lying areas.
People have also been advised to avoid public places and tourist destinations unless necessary, and not to touch electric poles or wires during rain. The administrations have urged the public to follow official advisories and take precautions.
For assistance or to report rain-related damage, the public can contact the District Emergency Operations Centre at the toll-free number 1077 or 0422-2306051. The control room operates round the clock.

Yellow alert remains in effect for heavy winds in coastal areas, western Wadden Islands
Saturday, 24 October 2026 - 16:25
The KNMI warns of heavy wind gusts in coastal areas, the western Wadden Islands, and the Limburg hills from Saturday evening until at least Sunday morning. A yellow alert is in effect in those locations, with gusts of 75 to 100 kilometers per hour expected, varying by place.
Since Friday evening, it has already been blowing quite hard in many parts of the country, causing storm damage, including trees falling onto cars and homes. From Saturday evening, low-pressure system Boelo will continue those strong winds.
On Saturday a code yellow weather warning for strong winds was in effect in Zuid-Holland, Zeeland, Limburg, Gelderland, Noord-Brabant, and Overijssel, following Storm Austen's arrival on Friday. Most severe winds came from the south.
The KNMI warns of traffic disruptions and breaking branches. Because trees are still “in full leaf,” many branches, including smaller ones, can break off, the weather institute said.
Sunday weather is set to be unsettled and windy, with frequent showers, especially in the north. Gusts will reach up to 90 km/h near the coast and on the Wadden Islands, while staying weaker inland. The temperatures will range from 12 to 15 degrees, with the highest readings in the southwest.
Reporting by ANP and NL Times

articles.title: Global Climate Emergency: Historic 30°C Pacific Heatwave Spares No Continent - The Sentinel - of this Land, for its People
articles.source: The Sentinel - of this Land, for its People
articles.full_text:
In a historic milestone for global climate monitoring, sea surface temperatures in the critical Niño 3.4 region of the central equatorial Pacific Ocean have crossed the 30°C threshold.
Data released by the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) confirmed that ocean temperatures hit 30.06°C, breaking the previous record of 29.82°C set during the 2015 El Niño. Ocean anomalies are now tracking up to 3.8°C above historical averages, an intensity unseen since modern record-keeping began.
Climate scientists warn that this supercharged thermal energy acts as a planetary "wrecking ball," worsening severe global disruptions. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) cautioned that the worst impacts are yet to come, as the climate event is expected to peak around December.
Highlighting the gravity of the phenomenon, WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo stated, "This is literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades. El Niño will peak towards the end of 2026, but its impacts will be felt long after that."
The unprecedented heat raises major warnings for upcoming severe weather, threatening intense droughts across Southeast Asia, disruptions to India's climate patterns, and extreme flooding in East Africa.
